questions.question: In the Windows operating system, _________ is the first user-mode process that initializes system sessions and starts essential background services.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Session Manager**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Session Manager Subsystem**, represented by the executable **smss.exe**, is the very first **user-mode process** started by the **Windows kernel** (ntoskrnl.exe) during the boot sequence.
 
• It is responsible for critical early-stage tasks such as creating **system-wide environment variables** and defining **symbolic links** for MS-DOS device names (like COM1 or LPT1).
 
• **Session Manager** initializes the **Windows subsystem** (win32k.sys and csrss.exe) and establishes the initial sessions, including **Session 0** for background services and the first interactive session for user login.
 
• Once the environment is ready, it launches the **Windows Logon Process** (**winlogon.exe**), which facilitates the user authentication interface and the subsequent loading of the user profile.
 
• If **smss.exe** terminates unexpectedly during system operation, it triggers a **Stop Error** or **Blue Screen of Death (BSOD)** because it is classified as a **critical system process**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Control Panel**

 
 
• A **centralized management utility** in Windows that provides a **graphical user interface (GUI)** for users to modify **hardware settings**, system configurations, and security policies.
 
• In modern versions of Windows, many of its functions are being migrated to the **Settings App**, though it remains a core part of the **Windows NT** architecture.
 
 
 
• **Windows Explorer**
 
 
• Also known as **File Explorer**, it acts as the **primary shell** of the operating system, providing the desktop interface and the hierarchical view for **file management**.
 
• It starts significantly later in the boot process than the Session Manager, specifically after a user successfully logs in via **Winlogon**.
 
 
 
• **Task Manager**
 
 
• A **system monitoring tool** (taskmgr.exe) used to view **real-time performance data** such as **CPU usage**, **RAM allocation**, and active **network throughput**.
 
• It allows users to manually manage **startup applications** and forcefully terminate non-responsive tasks or **background processes**.

questions.question: Which of the following cases for the first time held the Preamble to be part of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the landmark case of **Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)**, a **13-judge Constitutional Bench** of the Supreme Court held that the **Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution**.
 
• The Court explicitly overruled its previous stand in the **Berubari Union case (1960)**, declaring that the Preamble is not a mere introduction but a part of the constitutional structure.
 
• It observed that the Preamble serves as a guide to the **interpretation of the Constitution**, reflecting the grand and noble vision of the founding fathers.
 
• The judgment established the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, stating that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution under **Article 368**, it cannot alter the basic features mentioned or implied in the Preamble and the Constitution.
 
• The Preamble is neither a source of power to the legislature nor a prohibition upon the powers of the legislature; however, it is **justiciable** in the sense that the basic structure cannot be violated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Berubari Union Case (1960)**:

 
 
• In this case, the Supreme Court opined that the Preamble is the 'key to open the mind of the makers', but it is **not a part of the Constitution**.
 
• Consequently, it was held that the Preamble could not be used to override the specific provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Golaknath Case (1967)**:
 
 
• The Supreme Court held that **Fundamental Rights** are given a 'transcendental and immutable' position and Parliament cannot abridge or take them away.
 
• Although the Preamble was discussed as the 'soul' of the Constitution, the case did specifically address the Preamble's status as a 'part' in the way the 1973 judgment did.
 
 
 
• **S.R. Bommai Case (1994)**:
 
 
• The Supreme Court reaffirmed the **Kesavananda Bharati** ruling, stating that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
 
• It also declared that **Secularism** is one of the basic features of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following vehicles was used to launch the SpaDex mission by the Indian Space Research Organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PSLV-C60**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** has designated the **PSLV-C60** mission to carry out the **SpaDex** (Space Docking Experiment), which is a critical technology demonstrator.
 
• **SpaDex** is designed to test and validate **autonomous docking** and **undocking** capabilities, where two separate spacecraft modules join together in orbit.
 
• The mission involves two distinct spacecraft components—a **Chaser** and a **Target**—that will be launched together on the **PSLV-C60** and then separated to perform complex proximity maneuvers.
 
• This experiment is a foundational step for India's future space endeavors, specifically for the construction of the **Bharatiya Antariksha Station** (Indian Space Station) by **2035**.
 
• The **PSLV** (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is chosen for this mission due to its high reliability and precision in injecting multiple payloads into specific **Low Earth Orbits (LEO)**.
 
• Mastering docking technology is essential for **crewed missions**, **in-orbit refueling**, and **satellite servicing**, as well as complex planetary missions like **Chandrayaan-4** for sample returns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Known as India's heaviest rocket, used for the **Chandrayaan-3** and **Gaganyaan** missions.
 
• Capable of carrying 4,000 kg class satellites into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
 
 
• **SSLV-D2**

• Successfully deployed the **EOS-07**, **Janus-1**, and **AzaadiSAT-2** satellites in February 2023.
 
 
 
• **GSLV Mk II**
 
 
• A three-stage launch vehicle equipped with an indigenous **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)**.
 
• Primarily used for launching **INSAT** and **GSAT** series communication satellites.

questions.question: Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar M. Yaghi were awarded with Nobel Prize in 2025 for their contributions in which field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemistry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry** was awarded to **Susumu Kitagawa**, **Richard Robson**, and **Omar M. Yaghi** for their pioneering work in the development and advancement of **Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs)**.
 
• **Omar M. Yaghi**, a professor at the **University of California, Berkeley**, is widely credited with establishing the field of **Reticular Chemistry**, which involves linking molecular building blocks into strong, crystalline, and highly porous structures.
 
• **Susumu Kitagawa** of **Kyoto University** was recognized for his discovery of **porous coordination polymers (PCPs)** and for demonstrating that these frameworks can be **dynamic and flexible**, allowing them to selectively recognize and store specific molecules.
 
• **Richard Robson** from the **University of Melbourne** provided the foundational architectural principles in the late **1980s** and early **1990s**, predicting that **coordination polymers** could be engineered to have predictable, **open-network structures**.
 
• The discovery of **MOFs** revolutionized materials science by creating substances with the highest known **internal surface areas** (sometimes exceeding 7,000 square meters per gram), which are essential for **gas storage** and **molecular separation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs):**

 
 
• **Structural Features:** Composed of **metal ions** or clusters coordinated to **organic ligands** to form one-, two-, or three-dimensional lattices.
 
• **Carbon Capture:** MOFs are used to selectively **adsorb CO₂** from industrial flue gases, helping to mitigate **climate change**.
 
• **Water Harvesting:** Specifically developed **MOF-303** can extract potable **water from desert air** with low humidity levels using **solar energy**.
 
• **Hydrogen Storage:** They provide a safe and efficient medium for storing **hydrogen fuel** at lower pressures for **clean energy vehicles**.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Nobel Categories:**
 
 
• **Physics:** This prize typically honors discoveries in **quantum mechanics**, **astrophysics**, or **particle physics**, rather than molecular synthesis.
 
• **Medicine:** Focuses on **physiology**, **genetics**, or **biomedical breakthroughs** like **mRNA vaccines** or **CRISPR** technology.
 
• **Economic Sciences:** Officially known as the **Sveriges Riksbank Prize**, it recognizes contributions to **economic theory** and **social sciences**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical change only?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crystallization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **physical change** is a type of change in which only the **physical properties** of a substance, such as its shape, size, state, or color, undergo a transformation while the **chemical composition** remains identical.
 
• **Crystallization** is the process of forming solid **crystals** from a solution, melt, or gas. This occurs when a **solute** precipitates out of a solution, arranging its atoms or molecules into a highly ordered **lattice structure**.
 
• During **crystallization**, no new chemical substance is created; the substance simply transitions from a liquid or dissolved state into a solid state. For example, obtaining **pure copper sulfate** from an impure sample is a classic physical process.
 
• This method is predominantly used as a **purification technique** in laboratories and industrial processes because it allows for the separation of a solid from its **saturated solution** without altering its internal chemical identity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation**:

 
 
• It is a **chemical change** that involves the loss of electrons or an increase in the **oxidation state** of an atom or molecule.
 
• A common example is **rusting**, where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form **Iron(III) Oxide** (**Fe₂O₃**).
 
 
 
• **Combustion**:
 
 
• This is an **exothermic chemical reaction** between a fuel and an oxidant (usually **Oxygen**) that produces heat and light.
 
• It results in the formation of entirely new substances, such as **Carbon Dioxide** (**CO₂**) and **Water** (**H₂O**), making it an irreversible chemical change.
 
 
 
• **Reduction**:
 
 
• A **chemical process** characterized by the gain of electrons or the removal of oxygen from a compound.
 
• It is the functional opposite of **oxidation** and is a vital step in the **extraction of metals** from their naturally occurring ores.

questions.question: The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, does NOT propose to amend which of the following Acts?

options.text: Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Representation of the People Act, 1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **December 17, 2024**, by the Union Minister of Law and Justice to facilitate **simultaneous elections** (One Nation, One Election).
 
• The Bill specifically proposes amendments to the **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991** to synchronize the term of the **Delhi Legislative Assembly** with that of the **Lok Sabha**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It proposes to amend the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**, ensuring that the legislative cycle of the **Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir** aligns with the national electoral calendar. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The Bill also targets the **Government of Union Territories Act, 1963**, which governs the administration and legislature of **Puducherry**, to enable concurrent polling for its assembly. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **Representation of the People Act, 1951**, which regulates the **conduct of elections**, **corrupt practices**, and **disqualifications** of members, is not proposed for amendment under this specific Bill. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Under the proposed framework, if a **UT Assembly** is dissolved prematurely, the new assembly will only serve for the **unexpired term** of the five-year cycle to maintain synchronization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acts Proposed for Amendment:**

 
 
• **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991:** This Act was enacted to supplement the provisions of the Constitution relating to the **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** for the **NCT of Delhi** under **Article 239AA**.
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019:** This landmark legislation bifurcated the erstwhile state into the **Union Territories** of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**, following the abrogation of **Article 370**.
 
• **Government of Union Territories Act, 1963:** This Act provides for the establishment of **Legislative Assemblies** and **Councils of Ministers** in certain Union Territories, including **Puducherry**.
 
• **Representation of the People Act, 1951:** Enacted under **Article 327**, it provides the actual machinery for conducting elections to the **Parliament** and **State Legislatures**. While separate amendments were introduced for this Act in **2024** (such as those concerning **paid news**), it is distinct from the **Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill**.

questions.question: Which of the following has NOT aided in Globalisation of the Indian economy?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Farm subsidies**__.

__
 
• **Farm subsidies** refer to domestic financial assistance provided by the government to farmers to stabilize prices and ensure **food security** for the nation.
 
• Unlike the other factors, these subsidies are internal fiscal tools designed to protect **domestic producers** from the volatility of international market prices and competition.
 
• In the context of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, large farm subsidies are often classified as **trade-distorting** measures because they can lead to overproduction and artificially low prices, which hinders free global trade.
 
• While the **1991 Economic Reforms** focused on opening the Indian economy, farm subsidies remained a protectionist mechanism aimed at social welfare rather than a driver of **global integration**.
 
• The process of **Globalisation** is characterized by the free flow of capital, goods, and labor, whereas subsidies often function as a buffer that isolates domestic sectors from global market forces.

• **E-commerce**:

 
 
• Utilizes digital infrastructure to facilitate **cross-border transactions** and global market access for Indian enterprises.
 
• It has effectively minimized the **geographic distance** between local manufacturers and international consumers.
 
 
 
• **Reduction of Trade Barriers**:
 
 
• A core component of **Liberalisation**, involving the removal of **import licenses**, **quotas**, and high **tariffs**.
 
• This allowed foreign products and **capital** to flow more freely into the Indian market, increasing efficiency and competition.
 
 
 
• **Multinational Companies (MNCs)**:
 
 
• These organizations bring **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and advanced technology to India, creating jobs and enhancing local manufacturing capabilities.
 
• The presence of global brands like **Samsung**, **Hyundai**, and **Apple** integrates India into **Global Value Chains (GVCs)**.

questions.question: According to the Sustainable Development Report, 2025, what was India’s standing in the SDG Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025** is an annual global assessment that tracks the progress of all **193 UN Member States** toward the **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• In the **2025 SDG Index**, **India** secured the **99th** position, showing a marked improvement in its global standing compared to previous years where it ranked outside the top 100.
 
• The report is produced by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** and provides a score for each country based on its performance across **169 targets**.
 
• **India's** progress in **2025** is attributed to successful domestic policies like **National Green Hydrogen Mission** and **Swachh Bharat Mission**, which directly impact environmental and sanitation goals.
 
• The **SDG Index** score for **India** reflects its efforts to balance economic growth with environmental sustainability and social equity as part of the **2030 Agenda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• It was established in **2012** under the leadership of **Professor Jeffrey Sachs** to support the implementation of the **SDGs**.

• This internal monitoring helps **India** identify specific regions requiring intervention, contributing to its rise to the **99th** rank globally.

• The **2025** report marks a critical juncture as nations enter the final five-year countdown toward the **2030** deadline.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to form new states or alter their boundaries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 3** of the **Indian Constitution** vests the **Parliament** with the authority to undergo internal reorganization of the states of the **Union of India**.
 
• It empowers the legislature to form a **new state** by separating territory from any state, uniting two or more states, or joining any territory to a part of any state.
 
• The **Parliament** can also use this article to **increase or diminish the area**, **alter the boundaries**, or **change the name** of any existing state through a **simple majority**.
 
• A bill intended for these purposes can only be introduced in either House of **Parliament** with the **prior recommendation of the President**.
 
• If the bill affects the area, boundary, or name of a state, the **President** must refer the bill to the relevant **State Legislature** for its views within a specified period, though the **Parliament** is not legally bound by those views.
 
• This article highlights the **unitary tilt** of the Indian federal system, where the **territorial integrity** of states is not guaranteed by the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 2**:

 
 
• Relates to the **admission or establishment** of new states that are **not part** of the Union of India.
 
• It was notably used during the admission of **Sikkim** into the Indian Union via the **36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975**.
 
 
 
• **Article 5**:
 
 
• Deals with **citizenship** at the commencement of the Constitution on **January 26, 1950**.
 
• It covers persons who were born in India, whose parents were born in India, or who were **ordinarily resident** in India for five years preceding the commencement.
 
 
 
• **Article 6**:
 
 
• Confers **citizenship rights** to individuals who migrated to **India from Pakistan** before the specified cutoff date.
 
 
 
• **Article 4**:
 
 
• Mandates that laws made under **Article 2** and **Article 3** provide for the amendment of the **First Schedule** and **Fourth Schedule** without being considered formal amendments under **Article 368**.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) targeted _____________.

options.text: Indian-language newspapers critical of British rule
Hindi educational journals during British rule

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian-language newspapers critical of British rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act of 1878** was a restrictive law enacted by the British administration to curtail the freedom of the **Indian-language (vernacular) press**.
 
• Introduced by **Lord Lytton**, the then **Viceroy of India** (1876–1880), the act was primarily designed to suppress the growing **nationalist sentiment** and criticism of government policies in local languages.
 
• The legislation empowered **District Magistrates** to require publishers of vernacular newspapers to enter into a bond, pledging not to publish any material that could incite **disaffection** or hatred against the **British Crown**.
 
• If a newspaper violated the bond, the government had the authority to seize the **printing press** and other equipment without a court trial.
 
• A defining characteristic of this law was its **discriminatory nature**, as it was applicable only to newspapers published in Indian languages, while the **English-language press** was completely exempted from its provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context and Impact**:

 
 
• The act was a direct response to the scathing criticism of **Lord Lytton** regarding his handling of the **Great Famine of 1876–1878** and the costly **Second Anglo-Afghan War**.
 
• Due to its repressive nature, the law was widely condemned by Indian nationalists and was nicknamed the **Gagging Act**.
 
• A famous incident related to this act involved the **Amrita Bazar Patrika**; to escape the legal trap, the newspaper converted from a bilingual (Bengali/English) weekly into a purely **English-language** publication overnight.
 
 
 
• **Repeal of the Act**:
 
 
• The act faced intense opposition from the Indian public and liberal politicians in Britain. It was eventually repealed in **1882** by the successor Viceroy, **Lord Ripon**.
 
• The repeal was part of **Lord Ripon’s** more liberal policy framework, which aimed to restore **freedom of the press** in India.

questions.question: Which period is associated with the Extremist phase of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905-1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The period between **1905 and 1919** is historically recognized as the **Extremist Phase** or the era of **Militant Nationalism** within the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** in **1905**, orchestrated by **Lord Curzon**, served as the primary catalyst that shifted the national movement from moderate constitutionalism to radical action.
 
• The movement was led by the famous trio **Lal-Bal-Pal**, consisting of **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, and **Bipin Chandra Pal**, along with the intellectual leadership of **Aurobindo Ghosh**.
 
• Unlike the previous phase, the **Extremists** demanded **Swaraj** (self-rule) as a right and utilized methods such as the **Swadeshi** movement, **Boycott** of foreign goods, and the promotion of **National Education**.
 
• Internal ideological friction led to the **Surat Split** in **1907**, where the **Indian National Congress** divided into two groups: the **Moderates** and the **Extremists**.
 
• The phase drew to a close around **1919** with the enactment of the **Government of India Act 1919** and the subsequent transition of leadership to **Mahatma Gandhi** following the **Rowlatt Act** and **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moderate Phase (1885-1905)**:

 
 
• Characterized by the leadership of **Dadabhai Naoroji**, **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, and **Pherozeshah Mehta**.
 
• Followed the policy of **3Ps**: **Prayers**, **Petitions**, and **Protests** to seek administrative reforms.
 
 
 
• **Gandhian Phase (1920-1947)**:
 
 
• Marked by the dominance of **Mahatma Gandhi** and the philosophy of **Satyagraha** (truth force) and **Ahimsa** (non-violence).
 
• Included massive pan-India movements such as the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, **Civil Disobedience Movement**, and the **Quit India Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Key Ideological Shifts**:
 
 
• While the **Moderates** believed in the essential sense of justice of the British, the **Extremists** believed that **British Rule** was inherently exploitative and could only be challenged through mass sacrifice and direct agitation.
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** popularized the slogan, '**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it**,' which became the anthem of this era.

questions.question: Which feature correctly describes the extremists’ use of religious symbolism?

options.text: Festivals were reorganised to discourage participation from non-Hindu groups
Ritual worship was introduced into political meetings to replace speeches.
Cultural symbols like Shivaji and Ganapati were used for political mobilisation.
All movements were confined exclusively to Hindu religious gatherings.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cultural symbols like Shivaji and Ganapati were used for political mobilisation.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Extremist** phase of the Indian national movement (roughly **1905−1919**) was characterised by a shift from the constitutional methods of the Moderates to more radical forms of mass agitation and political mobilisation.
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, a prominent leader of the **Garam Dal**, pioneered the use of traditional religious and cultural icons to bridge the gap between the western-educated elite and the common masses.
 
• In **1893**, Tilak transformed the **Ganapati Festival** from a private domestic ritual into a grand **sarvajanik** (public) event in **Maharashtra**. This allowed for large gatherings where patriotic songs were sung and nationalist ideas were disseminated despite British bans on political meetings.
 
• In **1895**, he introduced the **Shivaji Festival** to commemorate the birth anniversary of the Maratha ruler **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj**. The objective was to invoke a sense of pride and a spirit of resistance against foreign rule by highlighting Shivaji as a national hero.
 
• These cultural symbols served as a powerful medium for **political mobilisation**, enabling the extremist leadership to reach the rural population and urban working classes who identified strongly with these religious and historical traditions.

questions.question: What is the main characteristic of cells in the meristematic phase of growth in plants?

The correct answer is __**Active cell division**__.

• The **meristematic phase** represents the earliest stage of plant growth, occurring primarily at the **root apex** and **shoot apex**, where cells are constantly undergoing **mitotic division**.
 
• Cells in this phase are characterized by having a **dense protoplasm** and **large, prominent nuclei**, which are essential for managing the high metabolic demands of frequent replication.
 
• The **cell walls** of meristematic cells are **primary** in nature, meaning they are **thin**, elastic, and composed mainly of **cellulose** to allow for expansion and division.
 
• These cells maintain rich **plasmadesmatal connections**, facilitating the rapid transfer of molecules and signals between adjacent actively dividing cells.
 
• A high **metabolic rate** is a hallmark of this phase, as the plant prioritizes the production of new cellular components over storage or structural maturation.

• Comparison with other growth phases:
 
 
• **Elongation Phase**: In this zone, cells undergo **increased vacuolation**. This is where **large vacuoles** begin to form, driving the physical lengthening of the cell through turgor pressure.
 
• **Maturation Phase**: Cells in this region achieve their **maximum size**. This phase is characterized by significant **cell wall thickening** and specialized protoplasmic modifications to perform specific permanent functions.
 
 
 
• Cellular structures in Meristems:
 
 
• **Vacuoles**: In the meristematic phase, vacuoles are typically **absent** or extremely small, as the cell volume is occupied mostly by cytoplasm and the nucleus.
 
• **Intercellular Spaces**: Meristematic tissues usually lack **intercellular spaces**, presenting a compact arrangement that supports structural integrity during rapid growth.

questions.question: In which of the following Indian states does the maximum portion of the Upper Ganga Plain extend?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Upper Ganga Plain** is a distinct physiographic sub-region of the **Indo-Gangetic Plain**, situated between the **Yamuna River** in the west and the **100-meter contour line** in the east.
 
• The maximum portion of this plain extends across the state of **Uttar Pradesh**, specifically covering its western and central districts, encompassing an area of approximately **1,49,000 square kilometers**.
 
• Geographically, it is bounded by the **Siwalik Range** to the north and the **Peninsular Plateau** (Bundelkhand) to the south.
 
• The region is subdivided into three major micro-regions: the **Ganga-Yamuna Doab**, the **Rohilkhand Plain**, and parts of the **Avadh Plain**.
 
• The topography is largely flat, formed by **Pleistocene** and **Holocene** alluvial deposits brought down by the **Ganga**, **Yamuna**, **Ramganga**, and **Sharda** rivers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Middle Ganga Plain**:

 
 
• This region starts from the **100-meter contour line** and extends eastward to the **Bihar-West Bengal** border.
 
• It primarily covers eastern **Uttar Pradesh** and the entire state of **Bihar**.
 
 
 
• **Lower Ganga Plain**:
 
 
• This section extends from the foot of the **Darjeeling Himalayas** to the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• It is located almost entirely within the state of **West Bengal** and includes the massive **Sunderbans Delta**.
 
 
 
• **Soil and Agriculture**:
 
 
• The Upper Ganga Plain is dominated by **Bhangar** (older alluvium) and **Khadar** (newer alluvium) soils.
 
• Due to fertile **Alluvial soil** and extensive **Canal Irrigation**, it is a leading producer of **Wheat**, **Sugar cane**, and **Rice**.
 
 
 
• **Haryana**:
 
 
• While some parts of eastern **Haryana** touch the **Yamuna** boundary, the state is predominantly categorized under the **Indo-Gangetic Divide** or the **Punjab-Haryana Plain**, separating the **Indus** and **Ganga** river systems.

questions.question: In which kind of forest do the plants remain leafless for most of the year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical thorn forest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical thorn forests** are characteristic of regions that receive less than **70 cm** of annual rainfall, indicating extreme **arid** or semi-arid conditions.
 
• These forests are primarily located in the north-western parts of India, spanning the states of **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, **Punjab**, **Haryana**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The vegetation is specially adapted to conserve water; the plants often have long, **taproot systems** that penetrate deep into the ground to reach the water table.
 
• A defining feature of these forests is that many plants remain **leafless** for a major part of the year to minimize water loss through **transpiration**.
 
• When leaves are present, they are typically small, thick, and **waxy**, or modified into **thorns** to discourage herbivores and further reduce evaporation.
 
• Common flora found in this ecosystem includes **Acacia**, **Euphorbias**, **Palms**, and various types of **Cacti**, many of which have **succulent stems** for water storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montane forest**:

 
 
• These occur in high-altitude mountain regions like the **Himalayas**, where vegetation changes from **broad-leaf evergreen** to **coniferous** trees (like **Pine** and **Deodar**) as elevation increases.
 
 
 
• **Littoral and swamp forest**:
 
 
• Found in coastal and deltaic regions, these are also known as **Mangrove forests**.
 
• The **Sundari** trees of the **Ganga-Brahmaputra delta** are a prime example, known for their **pneumatophores** or breathing roots.
 
 
 
• **Evergreen forests**:
 
 
• Found in areas with high rainfall (over **200 cm**), such as the **Western Ghats** and **North-East India**.
 
• The trees do not have a specific **shedding season**, ensuring the forest remains green throughout the year.

questions.question: What minimum distance should the reflecting surface be for an echo to be heard?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17.2 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sensation of any sound persists in the human brain for a duration of approximately **0.1 seconds**. This biological phenomenon is known as the **persistence of hearing**.
 
• To hear a distinct **echo**, the reflected sound must reach the observer at least **0.1 seconds** after the original sound is produced.
 
• The speed of sound in air varies with temperature; however, at a standard room temperature of **22°C**, the speed of sound is approximately **344 m/s**.
 
• The total distance traveled by the sound wave from the source to the obstacle and back to the ear is calculated by the formula: **Total Distance = Speed × Time**.
 
• By substituting the standard values, the total distance required is **344 m/s × 0.1 s = 34.4 m**.
 
• Since this represents the round-trip distance, the actual minimum distance between the **source of sound** and the **reflecting surface** is half of this value: **34.4 m ÷ 2 = 17.2 m**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Echo:**

 
 
• **Temperature:** As the temperature of the air increases, the **speed of sound** also increases. Consequently, the minimum distance required to hear an echo will be slightly larger on a hot day compared to a cold day.
 
• **Medium:** The speed of sound is different in different media (solid, liquid, gas). For instance, sound travels much faster in **seawater** (approx. 1531 m/s), requiring a much larger distance for an echo.
 
 
 
• **Reflection Laws:** Sound waves follow the **laws of reflection**, meaning they bounce off large, hard obstacles like **mountains**, high-rise buildings, or cave walls.
 
• **Reverberation:** This occurs when the reflecting surface is less than **17.2 m** away. The reflections reach the ear too quickly (less than 0.1s), causing the original sound to appear prolonged or **blurred** rather than a distinct repetition.

questions.question: Which of the following makes the Judiciary, the guardian of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judicial review**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicial review** is the foundational power of the **Judiciary** to examine the **constitutionality** of legislative enactments and executive orders of both the **Central** and **State governments**.
 
• This power ensures that the **Constitution** remains the **supreme law** of the land and that no branch of government violates the **Fundamental Rights** of the citizens.
 
• Under **Article 13** of the **Indian Constitution**, the judiciary has the mandate to declare any law **null and void** if it is found to be inconsistent with **Part III** (Fundamental Rights).
 
• The **Supreme Court** and the **High Courts** act as the **guardians** of the document by invoking **Article 32** and **Article 226** respectively to protect individual liberties against **unconstitutional** state actions.
 
• By exercising **judicial review**, the courts maintain the **federal equilibrium** and uphold the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, preventing the **Legislature** from exercising **arbitrary power**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence of the Judiciary**:

 
 
• Refers to the **autonomy** of the judicial branch, ensuring that judges can perform their duties without **political interference** from the **Executive** or **Legislature**.
 
• It is maintained through features like **security of tenure**, **fixed salaries**, and **Article 50**, which mandates the **separation of the judiciary from the executive**.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Overreach**:
 
 
• Describes a situation where the **judiciary** exceeds its constitutional limits and interferes in the **policy-making** or **administrative domain** belonging to the **Legislature** or **Executive**.
 
• While **Judicial Activism** is seen as a tool for **social justice**, **overreach** is often criticized as a violation of the **Separation of Powers**.
 
 
 
• **Service Conditions**:
 
 
• Includes the **appointment**, **salary**, **allowances**, and **pensions** of judges, which are charged on the **Consolidated Fund of India**.
 
• These conditions are protected and cannot be varied to a judge’s **disadvantage** after their appointment, except during a **Financial Emergency** under **Article 360**.

questions.question: Who were referred to as Uzhavar in Sangam literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ploughmen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the ancient **Tamil region**, social structure and agricultural hierarchies were extensively documented in **Sangam literature**, which encompasses works like the **Ettuthogai** and **Pattuppattu** composed between **300 BCE and 300 CE**.
 
• The term **Uzhavar** was used to denote the **ordinary ploughmen** who formed the backbone of the agrarian economy in the fertile **Marutam** (wetland) regions.
 
• These individuals were responsible for the actual tilling and cultivation of the soil, distinguishing them from the wealthier administrative or land-owning classes of the period.
 
• Historical records, including **NCERT** guidelines on ancient Indian history, categorize the rural population of South India into three distinct groups: **Vellalar**, **Uzhavar**, and **Adimai**.
 
• The **Uzhavar** played a critical role in the prosperity of the **Chola**, **Chera**, and **Pandya** dynasties by ensuring a steady supply of food grains, primarily rice, which was the staple crop.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Large landowners**:

 
 
• In the Tamil social hierarchy, they were known as **Vellalar**.
 
• They often held high positions in the royal administration and served as local village headmen or **Velis**.
 
 
 
• **Slaves**:
 
 
• Known as **Adimai**, they occupied the lowest tier of the social strata and were often attached to the land of the **Vellalar**.
 
• They worked alongside **Kadaisiyar**, who were defined as **landless labourers**.
 
 
 
• **Priests**:
 
 
• Often referred to as **Anthanar** in later Sangam layers, they were respected for their knowledge of rituals and sacred texts.
 
• They acted as advisors to the **Arasar** (kings) and played a role in the performance of **Vedic sacrifices**.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, the ‘Right to Freedom’ is specifically guaranteed under which exact set of Articles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 19, 20, 21 and 22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Freedom** is one of the six fundamental rights recognized by the **Constitution of India**, specifically detailed under **Articles 19 to 22** in **Part III**.
 
• **Article 19** guarantees citizens six specific freedoms: **Freedom of speech and expression**, peaceful assembly without arms, formation of **associations or unions**, free movement throughout India, **residence and settlement** in any part of the territory, and the practice of any **profession, occupation, trade, or business**.
 
• **Article 20** provides protection against **arbitrary and excessive punishment** to an accused person, whether a citizen or a foreigner. It includes clauses against **ex-post-facto laws**, **double jeopardy**, and **self-incrimination**.
 
• **Article 21** declares that no person shall be deprived of their **life or personal liberty** except according to the **procedure established by law**. This article is considered the most evolved and fundamental, covering rights like the **right to privacy** and **right to a clean environment**.
 
• **Article 22** deals with **protection against arrest and detention** in certain cases. It ensures that arrested individuals are informed of the **grounds of arrest**, allowed to consult **legal practitioners**, and produced before a **Magistrate** within 24 hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality (Articles 14–18)**:

 
 
• This cluster ensures **equality before the law** and equal protection of the laws (Article 14), prohibits discrimination (Article 15), and provides **equality of opportunity** in public employment (Article 16).
 
• It also includes the **abolition of untouchability** (Article 17) and the abolition of titles (Article 18).
 
 
 
• **Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)**:
 
 
• **Article 23** prohibits **human trafficking** and **forced labor (Begar)**.
 
• **Article 24** forbids the employment of children below the age of 14 in **hazardous factories** or mines.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)**:
 
 
• This set guarantees the **freedom of conscience** and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate any religion of choice.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies (Articles 32–35)**:
 
 
• **Article 32** allows citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of fundamental rights via writs like **Habeas Corpus** and **Quo-Warranto**.

questions.question: The primary focus of tertiary activities is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Production of intangible goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tertiary activities**, often referred to as the **service sector**, involve the provision of services rather than the production of tangible physical commodities.
 
• The primary focus of this sector is the **production of intangible goods**, which are services that provide utility and value but do not have a physical form, such as **expertise**, **labor**, and **advice**.
 
• These activities facilitate the smooth functioning of the economy by providing essential support to the **Primary** and **Secondary sectors** through infrastructure and logistics.
 
• Key examples of tertiary services include **transportation**, **banking**, **insurance**, **tourism**, **healthcare**, and **education**.
 
• Unlike manufacturing, the output of the tertiary sector is usually **consumed at the point of production** and cannot be stored for future use.
 
• In modern developed economies, the tertiary sector often accounts for the largest share of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** and employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Sector**:

 
 
• Involves the **extraction of natural resources** directly from the earth.
 
• Includes activities such as **agriculture**, **mining**, **fishing**, and **forestry**.
 
• It provides the **raw materials** necessary for industrial processes.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector**:
 
 
• Focuses on the **transformation of raw materials** into finished or semi-finished products.
 
• Includes **manufacturing**, **construction**, and **power generation**.
 
• It adds value to natural resources by changing their physical form through industrial labor and machinery.
 
 
 
• **Quaternary and Quinary Activities**:
 
 
• **Quaternary activities** are specialized tertiary services involving **information technology**, **research and development (R&D)**, and **knowledge-based** services.
 
• **Quinary activities** involve high-level decision-making by **executives**, **government officials**, and **consultants** who formulate policies and strategies.
